name: Low-Speed Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 and Class 3 pedal-assist up to 20 and 28 mph, and Class 2 motor-propelled up to 20 mph.

restrictions.rule: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and a motor of less than 750 watts (Illinois Vehicle Code §1-140.10)

Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals and stops at 20 mph; Class 2's motor can propel it alone, up to 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph (Illinois Vehicle Code §1-140.10)
Class 2's motor must cut out when the brakes are applied; Class 1 and Class 3 motors must cut out when the rider stops pedaling (Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1517)
Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour (Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1517)
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512) (Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1517)

Carries a permanent label, in at least 9-point Arial, stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; no one may knowingly change its speed capability or motor engagement without replacing the label (Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1517)
Class 3 riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers (Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1517)

Class 1 and Class 2 riders must also be 15 or older, and a rider under 18 may carry a passenger only if the passenger is their sibling, stepsibling, child or stepchild (Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1517, as amended by SB 3484 (2026))
Follows the bicycle rules of the road and may be ridden on any road open to bicycles, including bike lanes (Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1517)
May not be ridden on a sidewalk (Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1517)
Allowed on bicycle paths unless the municipality, county or local authority in charge bans it or a class of it (Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1517)

Allowed on bicycle paths unless the state agency in charge, the Department of Natural Resources on its land, or a park, forest preserve, conservation or transit district restricts it (Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1517, as amended by SB 3484 (2026))
Local authorities may regulate it, including requiring local registration and licensing
No other unit of local government, home-rule units included, may regulate it (Illinois Vehicle Code §11-1517, as amended by SB 3484 (2026))
Not a motor vehicle, moped or motor driven cycle: no driver's license, title or state registration (Illinois Vehicle Code §1-140.10)

An electric bicycle that doesn't meet this definition is a motor driven cycle, which needs a driver's license and is barred from sidewalks, bike lanes, bicycle paths and bike trails (Illinois Vehicle Code §1-140.10, as amended by SB 3484 (2026))
